questions.q: What are the three named pillars of the target architecture this lesson defines?
options: A new SIEM, a new firewall vendor, and a new ticketing system
A segmented OT/IT boundary, a consolidated Azure/AWS identity view, and an automated, queryable access inventory
A password policy, an awareness campaign, and a vendor risk review
A single pillar: full enterprise zero trust
questions.explain: The target architecture names three destinations: a segmented OT/SCADA boundary, one federated identity view across Entra ID and AWS, and an automated inventory that keeps the answer to 'who has access' always current.

questions.q: What is the target state described for pillar one, the OT/IT boundary?
options: Faster network speeds between corporate IT and SCADA
No traffic reaches the OT/SCADA segment unless a specific, documented rule allows it, replacing the current implicit-trust flat network
Moving SCADA systems entirely off the network
Doubling the number of firewalls without changing any rules
questions.explain: The target state replaces the flat network's implicit any-to-any trust with an explicit allow-list where every permitted path has a documented reason.

questions.q: Why are the three pillars sequenced rather than treated as independent, parallel projects?
options: Because Hartwell only has budget for one project at a time

Because segmentation makes the boundary worth consolidating identity around, the identity view gives the automation one coherent source to query, and the automation makes the whole architecture provable
Because the board required them to be done in alphabetical order
There's no real dependency; they were sequenced arbitrarily
questions.explain: Each pillar depends on the one before it: segmentation gives the identity view a boundary worth having, the consolidated identity view gives the automation one source to query, and the automation proves the resulting architecture actually matches reality.

questions.q: What is pillar two's target state for identity?
options: Deleting all AWS IAM accounts entirely
AWS IAM Identity Center federated to Entra ID, so Entra ID becomes the single identity plane and AWS access follows from Entra ID group membership
Creating a fourth, separate identity system to mediate between the other two
Letting each AWS account continue managing its own IAM users independently, just with better documentation
questions.explain: The target architecture federates AWS IAM Identity Center to Entra ID, making Entra ID the single place identity lifecycle events happen, with AWS access following from that one source.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the automated inventory pillar matters beyond simple convenience?
options: It saves Mara a few minutes of typing each week

It's the artifact that will later let Mara, a compliance audit, and the SIEM each independently check whether the access the architecture describes matches reality — the exact mechanism this capstone returns to later
It replaces the need for any human security review ever again
It has no further significance beyond this lesson
questions.explain: The automated inventory is what makes the architecture provable rather than just documented — later lessons in this capstone directly depend on this inventory existing and being queryable.
